metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent successfully used =PROPER(TRIM(B2)) formula to clean all 28 movie titles from column B into column C, saved the file.
metadata.capability_extraction: Enter PROPER/TRIM formulas, fill down ranges, apply cell formatting (bold), save file
metadata.explanation: Chains the original title-cleaning task with bold formatting on the header row. Evaluator checks C2='Minions In Black' (0.25) and C3='The Dragon With The Girl Tattoo' (0.25) for title-cleaning correctness, plus both A1 (Garbage Movie Titles header) and C1 (Clean Movie Titles header) are bold (0.5). The getter reads A1 bold, C1 bold, C2 value, and C3 value. The metric uses expected values from the rules dict and requires both column headers to be bold to match the 'both column headers stand out' requirement. [Fixed: removed truncated-hash stub files __771ce452.py; extended getter to read A1 bold and C3 value; updated metric to require both A1+C1 bold and add C3 spot-check; fixed metric to use expected.get('c1_bold_expected') instead of hardcoding True.]

Fix 2: Cleared metric stub check_bold_header__771ce452.py (truncated MD5 suffix) — full-hash file check_bold_header__771ce45281d75f3370a131f92752ad7a.py is the canonical implementation.
Fix 3: Extended getter to also read A1 bold status (Garbage Movie Titles header) and C3 value (second cleaning spot-check).
Fix 4: Updated metric to require both C1 and A1 bold for the 0.5 bold credit, matching the 'both column headers stand out' requirement in the instruction.
Fix 5: Split cleaning 0.5 credit into C2 (0.25) + C3 (0.25) to increase confidence that the entire column was processed.
Fix 6: Metric now reads c1_bold_expected and a1_bold_expected from expected dict instead of hardcoding True.
Fix 7: Added c3_expected and a1_bold_expected to task JSON expected rules.

scoring_breakdown.both_bold: 0.5 - Both A1 (Garbage Movie Titles header) and C1 (Clean Movie Titles header) have bold font

llm_judge_reasons: Bold coverage is now complete: getter reads both A1 (Garbage Movie Titles header) and C1 (Clean Movie Titles header) bold status; metric requires both to be True (from expected rules) before awarding the 0.5 bold credit. This directly matches the instruction's 'both column headers stand out' requirement.

Title-cleaning is verified with two representative spot-checks: C2='Minions In Black' (0.25) and C3='The Dragon With The Girl Tattoo' (0.25), providing reasonable confidence that the PROPER/TRIM transformation was applied correctly.

Correct expected.type='rule' parameter handling: metric uses expected.get('c2_expected'), expected.get('c3_expected'), expected.get('c1_bold_expected', True), and expected.get('a1_bold_expected', True), correctly treating expected as the rules dict directly.
Postconfig saves the file with Ctrl+S before the getter reads it, ensuring the openpyxl data_only=True read reflects the agent's actual changes.

Minor: Only 2 out of ~28 cleaned cells are spot-checked. A malicious agent could clean only C2 and C3 and leave the rest unchanged, earning full cleaning credit. This is an acceptable trade-off for practicality.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Consider adding one more spot-check cell (e.g., C5 or C10) to further reduce the chance of a partial-cleaning false positive, though this is optional given the current two-cell coverage.
